Name: IMV AG
Description:
Voxtrot was founded and is backed by an enthusiastic and mixed bunch of global entrepreneurs. The company uses its Swiss-based HQ to conquer the hearts of mobile users worldwide.

Voxtrot is a mobile network allowing you to make calls and send text messages for free from almost any smartphone anywhere in the world (in September 2010 we released our first Alpha Test version for smartphones running on Android OS)

Voxtrot uses the Internet to connect you to any other Voxtrotter in the world. Voxtrot works anywhere, whatever the carrying network (EDGE, GPRS, UMTS/3G, WiFi, etc.). Voxtrot does not interfere with applications on your phone or with the connection to your carrier. 

To use Voxtrot, simple, just dial a number or send text as you normally would. That's it. 
If your friend is also a Voxtrotter, then the call or text will be free. It's that simple. 
If your friend is not a Voxtrotter, you can still call through your carrier or send an invitation to join Voxtrot.

There is no catch. Voxtrot delivers state-of-art mobile communication services using unique 4th generation VoIP technology. Voxtrot just channels your voice through the Internet. That’s why you only pay for the use of data on your mobile device. If you have a good data plan, you stop paying for every call and text.

Why would you pay more than you have to?  Connecting to Voxtrot is free and doesn’t mean you would have to change phone, phone  number, or calling habits.

In the future, Voxtrot will offer calling packages for “out-calls” (i.e. calls to non-voxtrotters) and other great high added value premium services. Calls and texting between Voxtrotters will always remain free. By using cutting-edge internet-related technology we are able to keep our costs extremely low. This means free calls and texting for you.

To resume: Voxtrot is the mobile VoIP company that finally gets it right!

Description:

EMC was born in 1967 as cable TV operator and is focused today to build active System solution for the transmission of CATV signals. 

CATV Networks has an own History & Philosophy and are very different one to the other. The operational efficiency or QoS of each Network is given by several parameters. Every possibility to avoid huge technical changes or to simplify the actually "Status" is an opportunity to increase operating efficiency and reduce operating costs.

With this Goals we offer customer oriented solutions based on standard platforms. We support customers with a long term view, contributing step by step to their future oriented development. With every System we built and installed in the last 13 Years, a lot of Know How is at the disposal of our Customers.

What is our target:
Our Company main Goal is to allow a soft migration from HFC to a FTTx Network developing step by step the physical layer. 

In other words, EMC’s active System solutions permits to upgrade an HFC Network to FTTC, FTTB or FTTH, keeping DOCSIS and parallel or in a second step  prepare IP based services to be ready when the physical layer is transformed and the complete Network is ready for the technology jump to All over IP. 

We have patented and unique solutions for the access network oriented to the Down- and Upstream and the transport of QAM, RF and/or Docsis signals. It's a kind of “RF over Glass” but without need of optical splitter and without risk of “Optical Beat Interferences” like RFoG (Burst mode) Systems can generate. We know this technology since we installed such a solution in 2000, because there were no other physical possibilities. Now our customer will introduce Docsis 3.0 and we are looking to find a solution without limitations of Docsis 3.0 and 3.1 After 2000 we stopped offering RF-PON solutions like RFoG or DPON and developed our standard and safe solution.

Description:
CHASER is a collaborative research project funded by the CHIST-ERA programme of the European Union and dedicated to bringing unsupervised machine learning to wireless communication systems. This approach enables a wide range of location-based services without resorting to the spectrally costly and invasive traditional positioning methods.

The objective of CHASER is to develop methods and algorithms allowing to implement online, real time, network-wide channel charting, and to develop its predictive capabilities in real-world use cases. Ultimately, we envision channel charting as a service (CaaS), which assists a number of network functions and user-level applications with a pseudo-location management architecture accessible through a dedicated application programming interface.

The consortium involves Aalto University (Finland), Inria (France), ETH Zürich (Switzerland) and the University of Minho (Portugal).

Description:
The Wireless World Research Forum is a global organisation, which was founded in August 2001. We now have over 140 members from five continents, representing all sectors of the mobile communications industry and the research community.

The objective of the forum is to formulate visions on strategic future research directions in the wireless field, among industry and academia, and to generate, identify, and promote research areas and technical trends for mobile and wireless system technologies.

We are developing a common global vision for the future of wireless to drive research and standardization. In addition to influencing regional and national research programmes (such as the European Union’s FP7 programme) WWRF members contribute to the work done within the ITU, UMTS Forum, ETSI, 3GPP, 3GPP2, IETF, and other relevant bodies regarding commercial and standardisation issues derived from the research work.

The Forum is unique in bringing together industry and academia from across the globe in an active discussion of new concepts, algorithms and techniques. Members discuss how new insights will impact on provision in typical application areas and on value chains in the future. It provides a unique networking opportunity, and I strongly urge you to become a part of it, by attending our meetings, contributing to the work on the working groups, and by joining the Forum.

Name: International Telecommunication Union
Description:
The International Telecommunication Union (ITU) is the United Nations agency for digital technologies, driving innovation for people and the planet with 194 Member States and a membership of over 1,000 companies, universities, civil society, and international and regional organizations. 
Established in 1865, ITU coordinates the global use of the radio spectrum and satellite orbits, establishes international technology standards, drives universal connectivity and digital services, and is helping to make sure everyone benefits from sustainable digital transformation, including the most remote communities. 
From artificial intelligence to quantum, from satellites and submarine cables to advanced mobile and wireless broadband networks, ITU is committed to connecting the world and beyond.

Name: WSIS Process
Description:
The World Summit on the Information Society (WSIS) Forum represents the world's largest annual gathering of the ‘ICT for development’ community. The annual WSIS Forum is a global multi-stakeholder platform facilitating the implementation of the WSIS Action Lines for advancing sustainable development. The Forum provides an opportunity for information exchange, knowledge creation and sharing of best practices, while identifying emerging trends and fostering partnerships, taking into account the evolving Information and Knowledge Societies.

The WSIS Forum is constantly evolving and strengthening the alignment between the WSIS Action Lines and the Sustainable Development Goals. The Forum will serve as a key platform for discussing the role of ICTs as a means of implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals and targets, with due regard to the global mechanism for follow-up and review of the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

Name: Circet Switzerland
Description:
Circet ist der führende Anbieter von Infrastrukturdiensten für Telekommunikationsunternehmen in Europa. Das Unternehmen ist in einem boomenden Sektor tätig, der durch massive Investitionen für die Einführung von festen und mobilen Very High Speed-Breitbanddiensten unterstützt wird. Circet in der Schweiz

"Circet Switzerland, eine hundertprozentige Tochtergesellschaft von Circet, wurde 2020 mit dem Ziel gegründet, eine führende Position auf dem nationalen Schweizer Telekommunikationsinfrastrukturmarkt einzunehmen. Dank eines dynamischen und erfahrenen Teams und einer agilen Organisation wird die Schweizer Tochter die zahlreichen Möglichkeiten ausschöpfen, die sich für ihre Kunden bieten." - Denis Gheysen CEO

Wir streben in der Schweiz die Marktführerschaft an. Um dies zu erreichen, stützen wir uns auf drei Hauptpfeiler:

•	Als bester Arbeitgeber in unserem Bereich anerkannt zu werden, dank einer DNA, die Unternehmergeist, Fähigkeiten und dynamische Teams vereint.

•	In allen Regionen präsent zu sein, um nah am Kunden zu bleiben und eine optimale landesweite Abdeckung mit einer Organisation zu gewährleisten, die die unserer Kunden widerspiegelt.

•	Dank der Circet Academy können wir Talente anwerben, ausbilden und im Geschäft entwickeln. Theoretische und praktische Schulungen, Zertifizierungen und regelmässige Wissensaktualisierungen garantieren eine optimale Motivation unserer Teams und damit beste Qualität für unsere Kunden.
Wir profitieren von der Stärke einer grossen internationalen Gruppe und den in anderen Ländern gesammelten Erfahrungen, insbesondere bei der Digitalisierung von Prozessen. Dies ermöglicht es uns, unseren Kunden hochwertige und optimierte Dienstleistungen anzubieten.

Name: Broadband Commission for Sustainable Development
Description:
Established in 2010 by ITU, UNESCO, H.E. President Paul Kagame of Rwanda, and Mr. Carlos Slim Helu of Mexico, the Broadband Commission elevated the importance of broadband on the international policy agenda.

After fifteen years of advancing broadband connectivity through multistakeholder partnerships and advocacy, the Broadband Commission’s strategic framework, the Broadband Advocacy Targets, reached its expiration at the end of 2025.

The Commission set a valuable precedent for the importance of collaborative work to connect the unconnected. With over 100 knowledge products and 35+ multistakeholder Working Groups, the Commission issued more than 70 practical policy recommendations published across 15 editions of the annual flagship State of Broadband report.

We thank the dedicated Commissioners, External Experts, donors, our many partners and the Secretariat team.

Name: Schmid & Partner Engineering AG (SPEAG)
Description:
SPEAG – Schmid & Partner Engineering AG, Switzerland – is the leading developer and manufacturer of advanced, efficient, and reliable test equipment for the evaluation of near- and far-field electromagnetic radiation. Our smart, user-friendly, high-performance and -quality products are designed for precise measurements, ready for emerging 5G technologies, over a wide range of applications at frequencies of up to 110 GHz. SPEAG’s key products are: DASY8 – compliant specific absorption rate (SAR) measurements; cSAR3D – fast SAR testing; ICEy – automated near-field scanning for EM interference and compatibility (EMI/EMC); MAGPy – exposure assessments at below 10 MHz; DAK – dielectric measurement systems; EM Phantoms – body simulators for radiofrequency (RF) testing; and SEMCAD X – RF performance modeling in and on the human body.

SPEAG strives continually to meet the ever-increasing design, R&D, and production challenges related to complex emerging wireless devices. SPEAG forms the Zurich43 alliance together with its partner organizations the Foundation for Research on Information Technologies in Society (IT’IS), ZMT Zurich MedTech AG (ZMT), TI Solutions AG (TI Solutions), and the Z43 NetZero Foundation.

SPEAG – Empowering Innovation

Description:
Cucuyo's declared aim is to bring laser communication terminals to the market as an off-the-shelf product. There are major opportunities for this pioneering sector to deliver a significant part of the future generation of communications and services, because:

1. Digitalization is driving the ever-increasing amount of data and needed bandwidth transmitted in communication.
2. More frequently occurring climate catastrophes need secure and infrastructure independent communication.
3. The instable global situation needs uninterruptable and non-detectable connectivity.

Cucuyo solves critical communication issues of the fast-growing UAV market with by orders of magnitude increased data rates and make communication resilient to interference or jamming. Our original technology background comes from the German Aerospace Center DLR Oberpfaffenhofen. In the past our leading-expert team has already developed and flown many different types of laser communication systems for air, space, and stratosphere, having accumulated more than 50 years of experience in the field of laser communication.
